title: Denis (9 October)
hookLine: a stone bishop in Paris holds his own head in his hands
last: THE CROSS STANDS WHILE THE WORLD TURNS.

lines: A HILL AT THE EDGE OF PARIS.
cards: On the front of Notre-Dame in Paris, among the carved saints, stands a bishop in his robes. Where his head should be, there's nothing. His head is in his hands, held out in front of him, still wearing its miter.
Tourists photograph him and wonder. Parisians have a story ready, and it starts on a hill at the edge of their city, where the white church of Sacré-Cœur stands now. Today, Denis.

teach.b: Start with an early layer of the story, from Gregory of Tours, a bishop who wrote a history of the Franks.
He says Denis was sent to Gaul, to the town that would become Paris, as its bishop, and that he died by the sword for Christ.

Other old accounts fill in more: he preached, people came to faith, and in a time of persecution he was arrested with two companions, a priest named Rusticus and a deacon named Eleutherius, and all three were beheaded.
That's the core the Church keeps on his feast: Denis and companions, martyrs.

teach.h: THE LEGEND: HE CARRIED HIS HEAD.
teach.b: Then the legend grew. Later tellings say that after Denis was beheaded on the hill, he stood up, picked up his own head, and walked away, preaching as he went, until he reached the place where he wanted to be buried.
That's the bishop on the front of Notre-Dame. It's a story people tell, not a record. Some read it as a picture of how Parisians felt: their bishop was not finished by a sword.
And the hill? Tradition reads its name, Montmartre, as the mountain of martyrs. Historians debate where the name really comes from, but the story stuck to the place.

teach.h: NOT THE MAN PAUL MET IN ATHENS.
teach.b: In Acts, when Paul preaches in Athens, among those who believe is a man named Dionysius the Areopagite.
Medieval writers decided that Dionysius and Denis were the same man, Paul's convert sailing to Paris.
Today the Church treats them as two different saints: same name, different men, mixed together by people who loved them both.

how: Saint Denis and companions are remembered on 9 October; in France, and especially in Paris and at the basilica of Saint-Denis north of the city, the feast is kept with Mass.

games.q: you're a medieval writer. two saints are named Dionysius: Paul's convert in Athens and the bishop of Paris. what do you decide?
games.why: medieval writers merged them into one man; today the Church treats them as two different saints.

practice: Bring to mind France: Paris and its old churches, small villages with a bell tower in the center, and people of every faith and none who live there now, starting with anyone French you know.
If you pray, ask Denis, the bishop on the hill, to pray for the country he served; if you don't, simply hold its people in mind with good will.

wordCard.voice: Denis. Tradition calls him Paris's first bishop, beheaded with his companions on the hill the legend says he walked down, carrying his head.

carryVoice: Your line: the mountain of martyrs. A legend grew, and the hill kept the name. One thousand thirty-four days now.
